I am **Dmytro Mishkin**, a computer vision researcher and consultant based in Prague.

I did my PhD at [CTU in Prague](https://fel.cvut.cz/en) under the supervision of Prof. Jiri
Matas, on wide multiple baseline stereo and local features — the workhorse of 3D
reconstruction, SLAM and image retrieval. The thesis received the Dean's Prize and the
Rector's Prize, and reached the final of the Antonín Svoboda Award for the Best PhD Thesis.

I maintain the open source [Kornia](https://github.com/kornia/kornia) library, and I am a
co-author of [HardNet](https://github.com/DagnyT/hardnet),
[AffNet](https://github.com/ducha-aiki/affnet),
[LSUV initialization](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.06422),
[MODS](https://github.com/ducha-aiki/mods) and the
[Image Matching Challenge](https://vision.uvic.ca/image-matching-challenge/).
I co-founded the [Eastern European Computer Vision Conference](https://eecvc.com/) and the
Ukrainian research group Szkocka, and I serve
on the Expert Committee on Artificial Intelligence at the Ministry of Digital Transformation
of Ukraine.

This blog is where I write about computer vision, image matching, how research actually gets
done, and what AI is doing to the way we work. My full CV, publication list and talks live at
[dmytro.ai](https://dmytro.ai).
